items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: Jackie Robinson, I remember when he -- he didn't understand Paul Robeson at first.

ctx.x: We were talking about Paul Robeson.

Yeah, I realized in later years that this man sacrificed his whole career to make the white man aware of the Negro. Because Paul Robeson at this time was -- he was a brilliant actor, a brilliant singer, he was a Rhodes scholar, he was an all American football player, he was just everything. And he just killed himself, you know, his career. But in doing so he made the white man aware of the fact that he had to reckon with the black man. He just couldn't take him as Sambo, you know. He -- Jackie Robinson, I…
And I would catch him out in the court every now and then in Riverton and just talk to him, and it was just the man had a beautiful philosophy, he was a beautiful human being.
